newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-VIOLENCE MARS CHAMPIONS' CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VIOLENCE MARS CHAMPIONS' CUP TIE.

text.p: Egyptian club Zamalek made another violent return to Tunisia as fighting marred their African Champions' Cup defeat by CS Sfaxien on Sunday.
The match was stopped twice after players traded punches as CS Sfaxien scraped a 1-0 win in the semifinal, first leg tie at their home ground.
The match was one of six semifinal, first leg matches played in the three African club competitions at the weekend.

Zamalek, who were involved in ugly on-field fighting when they lost to Tunisian club Esperance in Tunis in the 1994 Champions' Cup final, had defender Nabil Mohamed sent off for a vicious elbow jab on an opponent that sparked off a two-minute stoppage in he second-half.
There was another break of some four minutes later after Medhat Abdelhadi brought down Sfaxien's Tunisian international Skander Souyeh and conceded a penalty with 10 minutes left to play.
The awarding of the penalty led to more on-field fighting and spectators rained down plastic bottles on to the pitch.
Souyeh converted the spot kick to give his side a narrow lead to take to the Egyptian coastal city of Alexandria for the return match on October 27.
A vital away goal by Sam Pam ensured a 1-1 draw for Nigeria's Shooting Stars in the other Champions' Cup semifinal on Friday against Algeria's JS Kabylie in Algiers.
The match was the first of two back-to-back cup ties at the July 5th stadium, which later saw CR Belouizdad also held to a 1-1 draw by Sodigraf of Zaire in their African Cup Winners' Cup tie.
Two former Cup Winners' Cup holders Arab Contractors of Egypt and Cameroon's Canon Yaounde met in their semifinal tie on Friday with Arab Contractors winning 2-1 at home.
A late goal from Essido ensured a fighting chance for Canon in the return match in Yaounde in two weeks' time.
Confederation of African Football (CAF) Cup holders Etoile Sahel of Tunisia won 2-0 in their semifinal, first leg match against Vita Club of Zaire in Sousse on Saturday.
Riad Jelassi scored an early goal for the hosts and Imed Ben Younes added a vital second midway through the second-half.
Kawkab Marrkesh of Morocco scored the biggest win of the weekend's matches with Redaoui scoring a hat-trick in their 4-1 home victory over Kenya Breweries on Sunday.
The return legs will all be played on the weekend of October 25-27.
